messages:
Alice: hitting a weird auth/config race with py-sdk async client + key rotation in 0.9.2. quick repro below, open to sanity check
Sam: can you paste the minimal repro?
Alice: yep — gist: https://gist.github.com/alice/rot-repro (short version)
Alice: ```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
import os, asyncio

async def worker(client):
    await client.generate("hello")

async def main():
    os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'KEY-A'
    a = AsyncClient()  # relies on env read
    b = AsyncClient()  # same pattern
    t1 = asyncio.create_task(worker(a))
    os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'KEY-B'  # rotate mid-flight
    t2 = asyncio.create_task(worker(b))
    await asyncio.gather(t1, t2)

asyncio.run(main())
```
Alice: observed: some requests still go out with OLD_API_KEY even though env changed earlier. reproducible ~20% on my laptop when running many tasks.
Jordan: that sounds like an auth header cache on the client side — do we build auth header once on init?
Sam: I think AsyncClient lazily reads credentials into an internal _auth_provider and then caches an Authorization header per connection pool. so rotation via env won't automatically update existing pooled connections.
Maya: yep this is also the contextvar/async race we saw in a different bug. if the sdk uses a contextvar for env fallback + connection pooling, rotation can get interleaved.
Ryan: thanks for the repro. short-term workaround: instantiate clients with explicit api_key param (e.g. AsyncClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) ) or call client.close() before rotation to drain pools.
Alice: workaround worked for me (passing api_key) — but it's awkward for apps that rely on central env rotation (k8s secrets update).
Jordan: we should add clear docs about credential precedence and mutation semantics (env vs explicit param). also we should consider exposing a reload_credentials() or an api on pool to refresh headers.
Sam: raising two things: 1) patch to avoid caching header at a scope larger than request, and 2) typing to make ApiKeyProvider explicit so callers know which objects are re-evaluated.
Maya: typing note: AsyncClient currently accepts Optional[str|Callable[[], str]] for api_key which is messy in stubs — propose a Protocol ApiKeyProvider with __call__ -> str. helps with static typing + injection.
Ryan: agree. I'll open a GH issue with repro and label sdk/py, bug, and perf. can someone drop the minimal gist into the issue?
Alice: done, pasted gist + stack trace + CI-ish timings.
devex-bot: CI check failed on branch feature/async-cred-reload — 2 tests failing (tests/auth_test.py::test_rotation, tests/pool_test.py::test_header_invalidation)
Sam: thanks @ryan — looks like the failing tests match this. Ryan can you add test-driven fix?
Ryan: on it. plan: add unit tests that simulate env rotation, then change pool to regenerate auth header per-request if provider is dynamic. keep fast path for static api_key.
Jordan: small UX ask — add a short FAQ entry in SDK docs: "How does key rotation work?" with examples of per-client explicit key, env-based clients, and recommended patterns for k8s secrets rollouts.
Maya: +1 on docs. also consider emitting a debug-level log when auth provider changes or when a header is refreshed (helps debugging in prod).
Alice: one more gotcha — I lost a few hours because my app used AsyncClient() in a module-level var and tests were flaky. note that module import time reading vs runtime matters. :facepalm:
Sam: classic. good to call out in onboarding sample apps that clients should be created in app startup code or passed in, not as a cold import global.
Ryan: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/issues/3423 — tagged @sdk-maintainer. I'll prototype fix + tests, then post a design PR for review.
Alice: thx all. if someone can review quick once the PR lands that would be great.
Jordan: happy to review the docs + typing change.
Maya: I'll add an integration test to the samples repo to cover secret rotation scenario in k8s-like env.
